name: NEW RIVER VALLEY COMMUNITY SERVICES
ai_summary: The auditor found that New River Valley Community Services' finance office was short-staffed in fiscal 2024, with two empty posts, one of them the Senior Finance Director for eight months. As a result, it filed its year-end report to the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services (DBHDS) six weeks after the extended deadline, and its 2024 single audit was 15 months late. Both findings concern money passed down by DBHDS, including Mental Health Block Grant and Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. The 2024 audit also reports a material weakness (a serious gap in financial controls) in the financial statements, and there were no findings in 2023.

name: COUNTY OF FLOYD
ai_summary: The auditor found that Floyd County's spending report for its Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds had key lines with no supporting records, and that the County's schedule of federal spending left out $175,000. Both problems were in the 2025 audit and affect money passed through the Department of Criminal Justice Services and the Department of Housing and Community Development. The County also has no purchasing manual that meets federal rules, which also affects school meal funds from the Department of Education. The 2024 and 2025 audits were each filed more than a year after the fiscal year ended, which is late.

name: SHENANDOAH AREA AGENCY ON AGING, INC
ai_summary: For the second audit in a row, the agency's year-end report to the Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services (DARS) had revenue and spending figures that did not match its own books. The cause both years was that staff did not check the report against the accounting records before sending it. The problem is limited to this one report for three aging programs, and no costs were questioned. The 2024 audit also reported a material weakness, meaning a serious control gap, in the financial statements, but the data gives no detail on it.

name: WYTHEVILLE REDEVELOPMENT & HOUSING AUTHORITY
ai_summary: The 2025 auditor found that about 44% of the tested Housing Choice Voucher and Mainstream Voucher files were missing required signatures from tenants or landlords. The auditor called this a material weakness, meaning a serious gap in controls, and linked it to turnover among executives and program staff. This is the only finding in 2023–2025, it is not a repeat, and no costs were questioned. The money comes straight from HUD, with no Virginia state agency in between. The 2025 and 2023 audits were both filed late.

name: Middle Peninsula Planning District Commission
ai_summary: The Commission's finance office lost staff and had no backup, so bank accounts were not reconciled on time and the yearly list of federal spending by grant was wrong until the auditor corrected it. The auditor rated all three 2024 problems as material weaknesses, the most serious kind of control gap. All three trace to the same cause and affect both federal programs passed down by the Department of Health and the Department of Transportation. The 2024 audit was filed 17 months after year end, and no 2023 or 2025 audit is on file.
